To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Zr1-xSi xO2 mixed oxides obtained using the sol-gel method have a mesoporous structure, with a local homogeneous distribution of the cations.
Zr and Si cations are interdispersed in Zr-Si mesoporous oxo matrices, and that the local structure of Zr and Si varies with the concentration of each cation.

the local homogeneous interdispersions of Zr and Si in mixed mesoporous oxide thin films can be assessed by using FTIR spectroscopy, and that the Zr and/or Si coordination, symmetry and chemical states can be determined by using XANES spectroscopic measurements.

the development of new mesoporous materials with a high degree of homogeneity in their chemical composition and with the understanding of the chemical environment of their atoms, which are essential properties for the design of new materials with improved properties.
the study of the interdispersion of Zr and Si in mixed mesoporous oxide thin films.

the Zr1-xSiox mixed oxides present a homogeneous interdispersion at the atomic scale of the Si and Zr cations.

in mixed Zr-Si mesostructured oxides, the Zr and the Si atoms are homogeneously interdispersed at the nanometric level, and the Si atoms occupy the tetrahedral coordination sites, while the Zr atoms are octahedrally coordinated.
the local structure and chemical environment of Zr and Si in mixed mesoporous oxide thin films are homogeneous and interdispersed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the local environment of both cations, Zr and Si, are homogeneous, which is a key factor to obtain mixed mesoporous materials with good properties.

the local homogeneous Zr and Si dispersion in the mixed oxide can be explained by the presence of Zr in SiO2 spaces and by the fact that Zr can be incorporated in the SiO2 network, even when it is present in low concentrations.
Zr1-xSxO2 mixed oxide thin films with a wide range of compositions were obtained by a simple and fast method.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of FTIR spectroscopy is not enough to determine the local environment of Zr in mixed oxide systems.
XANES can be used for the selective study of the local structure of specific atoms, even in the presence of other elements with similar chemical and electronic properties.
the local structure of the mixed oxides is not only dependent on the composition, but also on the synthesis conditions.
